title: Fabrication of a Biomimetic Nano-Matrix with Janus Base Nanotubes and Fibronectin for Stem Cell Adhesion
protocol: Prepare a solution containing 8.50 g of 2-cyanoacetic acid and 9.80 g of ethylcarbamate in 25 mL of toluene and 2.5 mL of N, N-dimethylformamide.
Add 4.90 mL of phosphoryl chloride dropwise to the prepared solution.
Heat the mixture to 70 °C and keep stirring for 1.5 h.
Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature and pour in 100 g of ice water.
Extract the aqueous layer with ethyl acetate (3 x 250 mL).
Wash with 100 mL of brine.
Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter and evaporate volatiles under vacuum to get a pale-yellow solid.
Subject the yellow solid to silica gel flash column chromatography (3% methanol/dichloromethane) to yield 15.61 g of compound A1 as a white powder.
Mix 3.12 g of compound A1 and 2.75 g of potassium carbonate in 50 mL of N, N-dimethylformamide.
Stir at room temperature for 2 h.
Add 2.6 mL of carbon disulfide to the reaction suspension.
Keep stirring for 4 h.
Add absolute ethanol to the reaction mixture at 0 °C.
Filter the yellow precipitate out and wash with diethyl ether.
Dry under vacuum overnight to yield 6.18 g of compound A2 as pale-yellow solid.
Add 2.7 mL of methyl iodide in 15 mL of acetonitrile.
Prepare a solution of compound A2 by adding 6.18 g of A2 to 80 mL of water/acetonitrile (7:3 ratio).
Mix both the solutions and stir at room temperature for 30 min.
Heat the reaction mixture to 95 °C and stir for 3 hours.
Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature.
Evaporate the volatiles under vacuum.
Extract the residue three times with 100 mL of ethyl acetate.
Wash the organic layer with brine.
Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate.
Filter the dried organic layer.
Evaporate the volatiles under vacuum to obtain a yellow solid.
Subject the yellow solid to silica gel flash column chromatography using 30% ethyl acetate/hexanes to yield compound A3 as a light-yellow solid.
Prepare allylamine solution by adding 925 µL of allylamine in 20 mL of ethanol.
Add the allylamine solution dropwise to the solution of compound A3 prepared with 3.14 g of A3 in 75 mL of absolute ethanol over 30 minutes.
Heat the reaction mixture to reflux for 16 hours.
Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature.
Evaporate the volatiles to give a yellow solid.
Subject the yellow solid to silica gel flash column chromatography using 50% ethyl acetate/hexanes to 2% methanol/dichloromethane to yield compound A4 as a white crystal.
Add 2.05 g of guanidinium hydrochloride and 7.8 mL of sodium ethoxide (21 wt% in ethanol) in 14 mL of absolute ethanol.
Heat the mixture to 45 °C for 15 minutes.
Filter off the insoluble material.
Add the filtrate directly into the solution of compound A4 prepared with 2.70 g of A4 in 40 mL absolute ethanol.
Heat the reaction mixture to reflux for 16 hours.
Filter the precipitate out to obtain 2.65 g of compound A5 as an off-white solid.
Add 24.9 mL of triethylamine slowly to the slurry mixture obtained by adding 2.11 g of compound A5 and 1.10 g of 4-Dimethylaminopyridine in 120 mL of tetrahydrofuran over 1 min.
Stir at room temperature for 2 min.
Add 20.7 mL of di-tert-butyl dicarbonate dropwise to the reaction mixture and keep stirring at room temperature for 40 h.
Add 20 mL of water to quench the reaction.
Evaporate the volatiles under vacuum.
Extract the red viscous residue with 500 mL of ethyl acetate.
Wash it in with 250 mL of water, 75 mL of 10% citric acid, and 200 mL of saturated sodium bicarbonate.
Wash again with 200 mL of brine.
Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter and evaporate the volatiles under vacuum to give a red/orange solid.
Subject the solid to silica gel flash column chromatography (0-20% ethyl acetate/hexanes) to yield 3.87 g of compound A6 as a white foam.
Add N-methylmorpholine N-oxide dropwise to the solution of compound A6 in acetone/water (8:1, 58.5 mL).
Stir at room temperature for 5 min.
Add osmium tetraoxide dropwise to the mixture over a period of 3 min and keep stirring at room temperature for 24 h.
Quench the reaction with 1.0 M aqueous sodium sulfite until the solution turns colorless.
Remove the volatiles under vacuum to result in a white slurry in water.
Extract the residue with 350 mL of dichloromethane.
Wash the extract with 150 mL of water.
Wash the extract with 150 mL of brine.
Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate.
Filter and evaporate the volatiles under vacuum to yield compound A7 as a white solid.
Add 760 g of sodium periodide to the mixture of 1.36 g of compound A7 in dichloromethane/water (6:1, 65 mL).
Stir at room temperature for 42 h.
Filter off the insoluble material and concentrate the filtrate under vacuum.
Extract the resulting residue with 250 mL of dichloromethane.
Wash the extract with 100 mL of water.
Wash the extract with 100 mL of brine.
Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate.
Filter and evaporate the volatiles under vacuum to give the crude product.
Subject the crude product to silica gel flash column chromatography (5-40% ethyl acetate/hexanes, then 5% methanol/dichloromethane) to yield compound A8.
Prepare a solution of 830 mg of compound A8 in 15 mL of 1,2-dichloroethane.

Add the solution dropwise to the mixture of 6-benzyloxycarbonylamino-2-L-amino-hexanoic acid trimethylsilyl ethyl ester (649.5 mg) and N,N-diisopropylethylamine (591 µL) in 24 mL of 1,2-dichloroethane over 3 min.
Stir at room temperature for 15 min.
Add 360.3 mg of sodium triacetoxyborohydride to the solution.
Stir the reaction mixture at room temperature for 24 hours.
Quench the reaction mixture with 6 mL of water.
Extract the reaction mixture three times with 200 mL of dichloromethane.
Wash the extract twice with 200 mL of 10% citric acid in water.
Wash the extract twice with 200 mL of water.
Wash the extract once with 200 mL of saturated sodium bicarbonate solution.
Wash the extract once with 200 mL of brine.
Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate.
Filter and evaporate the volatiles under vacuum to obtain the crude product.
Subject the crude product to silica gel flash column chromatography using a gradient from 5-30% ethyl acetate/hexanes.
Collect fractions containing compound A9 and combine them.
Dissolve 0.54 g of compound A9 in 10 mL of 94% trifluoroacetic acid/thioanisole solution.
Stir the mixture at room temperature for 72 hours.
Add diethyl ether (80 mL) to the reaction mixture and centrifuge.
Pour out the clear trifluoroacetic acid containing supernatant.
Wash the precipitate with diethyl ether and methanol to yield crude JBNT monomer.
Purify the crude JBNT monomer by high-performance liquid chromatography using a reverse phase column.
Use solvent A: 100% water, solvent B: 100% acetonitrile, and solvent C: pH=1 HCl water solution.
Set the flow rate to 3 mL/min.
Collect the largest peak eluting at approximately 7.2 minutes.
Add 80 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNT aqueous solution to 40 µL of 1 mg/mL FN aqueous solution.
Pipette several times to mix.
Dilute 10 µL of 100 µg/mL FN with 40 µL of distilled water to make a 20 µg/mL solution of FN.
Prepare 100 mg/mL solution of JBNTs by diluting 5 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNTs in 45 µL of DI water.
Mix 10 µL of 100 µg/mL FN and 5 µL of 1 mg/mL of JBNTs in 35 µL of DI water to form the NM solution.
Coat three wells of a 96-well clear round bottom microplate with FN, JBNT solution, and NM solution respectively.
Each well receives 50 µL of the respective solution.
Freeze the plate at -80 °C overnight.
Turn on the lyophilization instrument and vacuum pump.
Press the cool down button to reduce the temperature of the system to -50 °C.
Place the frozen plate into the lyophilized instrument and close all openings.
Click the start button to reduce the system pressure to 0.9 mbar.
After 4 hours, press the aerate button to increase the system pressure to atmospheric pressure.
Take the plate out of the lyophilized instrument.
Observe the FN, JBNTs, and resulting self-assembled NM with a microscope.
Take photographs of the materials with a camera.
Mix 30 µL of 100 µg/mL FN with 15 µL of distilled water and 5 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNTs to prepare the JBNT/FN NM solution.
Pipette the solution several times until a white solid suspension is visible.
Dilute 5 µL of 1 mg/mL JBNTs with 45 µL of distilled water to prepare the JBNT control solution.
Dilute 30 µL of 100 µg/mL FN with 20 µL of distilled water to prepare the FN control solution.
Measure the UV-Vis absorption spectra of the FN, JBNT, and JBNT/FN NM solutions from 190 nm to 850 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Clean the test surface of the spectrophotometer.
Drop 2 µL of distilled water on the clean test surface for measuring as blank.
Clean the test surface of the spectrophotometer.
Drop 2 µL of JBNT solution on it.
Measure the absorption spectra of JBNT solution from 190 nm to 850 nm.
Clean the test surface of the spectrophotometer.
Drop 2 µL of JBNT/FN NM solution on it.
Measure the absorption spectra of JBNT/FN NM solution from 190 nm to 850 nm.
Clean several grids before negative staining with a basic plasma cleaner.
Drop 3 µL of 1 mg/mL of JBNTs aqueous solution on a grid and leave for 2 min.
Rinse each grid with 100 µL of 0.5% uranyl acetate (UA) solution.
Drain the excess solution from the grids with filter paper.
Air dry the grids at room temperature.
Drop 3 µL of JBNT/FN NM solution on a separate grid and leave for 2 min.
Rinse each grid with 100 µL of 0.5% uranyl acetate (UA) solution.
Drain the excess solution from the grids with filter paper.
Air dry the grids at room temperature.
Mix 9 µL of JBNT/FN NM solution with 3 µL of 2.0% UA solution and pipette it several times.
Pipette the mixed solution on the grids and keep it for 2 min.
Use a filter paper to remove the mixed solution from the grids.
Dry the grids at room temperature.
Characterize the specimen for JBNTs, JBNT/FN NM stained with step 5.2.1, and JBNT/FN NM stained with step 5.2.2 with the TEM.
Add 200 µL of negative controls (NC, PBS), JBNTs, FN and the JBNT/FN NM solutions into one well of an 8-well chambered slide, respectively.
Freeze dry the 8-well chambered coverglass with the lyophilized instrument to coat materials on the bottom of wells.
Add 10,000 cells/wells hMSCs (Passage 3) into the wells.
Incubate them for 24 h at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Pipette out the cell culture medium from the wells.
Rinse the culture with 1x PBS solution.
Add 100 µL of the fixative solution to each well with cells.
Leave for 5 min.
Rinse cells gently with 1x PBS twice.
Dilute 1% Triton-X 100 to 0.1%.
Add 100 µL of 0.1% Triton-X 100 to each well with cells.
Leave for 10 min.
Rinse cells gently with 1x PBS twice.
Dilute the Rhodamine Phalloidin to 1.65 µM.
Add 100 µL of Rhodamine Phalloidin to each well with cells.
Incubate the chambered coverglass keeping from light at room temperature for 30 min.
Rinse cells gently with 1x PBS twice.
Capture the cell images with a fluorescent microscope.
Count the cell numbers on fluorescent images for each group.
Calculate the cell adhesion density by averaging of three random areas in each well.
